source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Garware is described as the top exporter of paint protection film (PPF) globally, with over 80% of PPF exported to USA, South America, Russia, China and Europe. It competes against 3M, XPEL and Chinese player KDX Window Film in a globally competitive PPF/BOPET films market. No explicit China+1 supply-chain-diversification framing was found — exports reflect established global market leadership rather than a diversification narrative (and Garware itself exports into China).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Garware Hi-Tech Films is a net debt-free entity; total debt (lease liabilities and acceptances) fell to Rs 23.03 Cr in FY25 from Rs 30.36 Cr in FY24, with overall gearing of just 0.01x — minimal balance-sheet exposure to interest rate risk, though an exact floating-rate % was not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw materials PTA (Purified Terephthalic Acid) and MEG (Mono-ethylene glycol) are crude oil derivatives; the company mitigates price volatility via forward contracts and long-term agreements, and passes crude-linked cost changes to customers with a 1-2 quarter lag. Exact % of raw material cost tied to crude was not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Consolidated export revenue was ~77% of FY25 revenue of Rs 2,109 Cr, spanning 90+ countries with USA, Europe and Middle East as major markets. Currency-wise USD/EUR revenue split was not disclosed in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmed company-specific PLI participation was found. General industry commentary notes India's specialty polyester film / solar control sector broadly benefits from PLI-related policy support, but no direct disclosure of Garware receiving PLI incentives was located.

china_plus_one.evidence: Endurance exports to Europe, Latin America, Middle East and Asia with a two-wheeler component focus; European business turnover (in Euro terms) rose 10.1% YoY, with India's trade agreements with the EU, UK and US cited as supportive tailwinds. No explicit China+1 / supply-chain-diversification narrative was found — growth is framed around Endurance's own European subsidiary demand recovery, not a China+1 sourcing shift toward India.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Endurance held a net cash position as of March 2025 (net debt approximately -Rs 1,122.6 Cr); long-term debt was ~Rs 6 billion (FY25) vs ~Rs 5 billion (FY24), against ~Rs 11.2 billion cash. Net-cash entity with limited floating-rate exposure, though exact floating-rate % not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are aluminium and steel (die-casting/suspension/braking components), which are not crude-linked; rubber-based components have partial crude linkage via the synthetic rubber/petrochemical value chain. Exact raw-material cost % tied to crude was not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 consolidated revenue Rs 11,560.8 Cr (+12.9% YoY): India 75.8%, Europe (Endurance's own European subsidiaries) 23.6%, Maxwell (Brazil) 0.6%. Europe revenue is EUR-denominated; USD-specific revenue share not disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Endurance does not appear among publicly disclosed PLI-Auto scheme approved applicants found in available sources (OEM beneficiaries cited: Tata Motors, Bajaj Auto, M&H, TVS Motor, Ola Electric; component beneficiary cited: Toyota Kirloskar Auto Parts). No confirmed PLI participation or incentive revenue found for Endurance.

ABB.report_year: CY2024 (ABB India follows a January-December fiscal/calendar year)

china_plus_one.evidence: ABB India pursues a 'local for local' / 'Make in India' manufacturing strategy (new energy-efficient drives production line, localized MCB manufacturing with 700+ variants) aimed at serving the domestic market rather than an export-driven China+1 diversification narrative. Exports are only ~10% of business mix; no explicit China+1 framing was found.

govt_capex.evidence: Q4 CY2024 revenue growth was led by the Electrification division on data center orders and EPC (infrastructure) customer execution, and by Motion on traction drives/converters (rail-linked). This points to meaningful infrastructure/government-adjacent demand, but no explicit government/public-sector revenue % was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports account for approximately 10% of ABB India's business mix per management commentary on the Q4 CY2024 earnings call. CY2024 revenue was a record Rs 12,188 Cr (+17% YoY), with the substantial majority (~90%) domestic INR revenue; export currency mix not disclosed.

rural.evidence: Nestle India has pursued a 'RUrban' rural-expansion strategy since 2019, extending distribution into approximately 216,000 villages. Rural revenue contribution has been reported at varying levels (~18-25% of sales) across different periods/sources, below the broader FMCG industry rural average of over 35%; rural is described as 'one of the biggest growth opportunities' in company commentary. No single consistent FY24-25 rural revenue % was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Milk is Nestle India's largest raw material by cost, followed by green coffee, wheat, edible/palm oils and packaging materials; green coffee and milk prices remained elevated through FY25 while palm oil and wheat costs eased. Crude oil linkage is indirect (via packaging materials and edible oils) rather than a primary direct input; no specific % of raw material cost tied to crude was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export sales are a small share of total revenue: Q4 FY25 export sales of Rs 212.66 Cr vs domestic sales of Rs 5,235 Cr (~4% of quarterly sales); Q1 FY26 export sales of Rs 213.95 Cr vs domestic sales of Rs 4,860 Cr (~4.2%). FY25 full-year revenue was approximately Rs 19,089-20,078 Cr (figures vary by source); exports are consistently a small single-digit percentage of total sales.

rural.evidence: United Spirits' largest-volume segment is Indian Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL, e.g. McDowell's No.1), which has significant mass-market and semi-urban/rural distribution reach across India; no specific rural revenue % was disclosed in available sources.

rate_sensitive.evidence: United Spirits operated with effectively zero long-term debt as of FY25 (debt-to-equity ratio ~0.0 in both FY24 and FY25), against shareholder funds of Rs 8,104 Cr — a net-cash position with minimal floating-rate liability exposure, though an exact floating-rate % was not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA, roughly 40% of raw material cost, derived from sugar/grain feedstock) and glass bottles (glass prices rose 15-18% over recent years) — together roughly half of raw material cost. These inputs are agri- and silica-based rather than directly crude oil-linked; no significant crude oil raw-material exposure was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: United Spirits distributes imported Scotch whisky and other brands via parent Diageo's global portfolio, alongside its own export subsidiary Shaw Wallace Overseas Limited (SWOL), which exports products to 35+ countries including the UK, US, Australia and Singapore. Specific USD revenue % and hedging policy were not found in available sources.

rural.evidence: Four-year revenue CAGR of Tier-III and beyond cities was 17% vs 14% overall CAGR for the same period, with these smaller cities now contributing approximately 3% of Dr Lal PathLabs' revenues (per FY25 results commentary).

inr_exposure.evidence: International presence remains marginal, limited to operated laboratories and partnerships in Saudi Arabia, UAE, Nigeria, Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri Lanka, plus sample referrals from ~15 countries mainly for NRI testing; these arrangements do not form a significant revenue contributor. Regional revenue split cited as North India ~45%, West ~25%, South ~15%, East ~10%, international ~5% of FY25 revenue.

FY25 consolidated revenue ~₹7,896-7,902 Cr (+18.6% YoY). International operations accounted for 54% of total revenue (domestic 46%), international business grew 20.5% YoY. Regional split: Emerging Markets revenue ₹1,510 Cr (+27.9% YoY, ~19% of total), Canada ₹1,252 Cr (+35.7% YoY, ~16% of total), Europe ₹1,474 Cr (+4.4% YoY, ~19% of total). Domestic revenue grew 16.4% YoY. No single 'USD revenue' figure disclosed; revenue is spread across CAD, EUR and emerging-market currencies in addition to USD.

pli_scheme.evidence: Emcure Pharma is one of 9 domestic pharmaceutical companies approved under Group B of the Government of India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (₹15,000 Cr scheme outlay), aimed at boosting domestic API/formulation manufacturing and reducing import dependence. Specific revenue contribution from PLI not disclosed in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Netweb positions itself around 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' (Self-Reliant India) import substitution rather than explicit China+1 framing: 'in-house capabilities in design, SMT, and production of cutting-edge enterprise-grade IT hardware aligned well with the government's vision of an Atmanirbhar Bharat.' Company holds verified Class-I supplier status under Public Procurement (Make in India) preference, and is 'the only listed Indian pure-play eligible for all central government, PSU and defence server tenders above Rs 50 crore where Dell, HPE and Lenovo do not qualify' -- indicating import-substitution rather than explicit China-plus-one revenue attribution.

govt_capex.evidence: Netweb Technologies' customer base breakdown cited as Government 42.8% vs Non-Government 57.2%; ~50% of business from Centre/high-end enterprises. Central government + PSU + defence server addressable market estimated at Rs 6,000-8,000 Cr annually.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue contribution was 9.0% in Q3 FY25 (used as full-year FY25 proxy; domestic ~91%). AI-related revenue contributed 14.8% of FY25 revenue, growing 112% YoY.

pli_scheme.evidence: Netweb Technologies received a PLI incentive of Rs 5,93,97,758 (~Rs 5.94 Cr) under the Government of India's PLI Scheme 2.0 for IT Hardware (period July 1, 2023 - March 31, 2024), awarded by MeitY, in recognition of its high-performance computing manufacturing. Incentive amount as % of total revenue not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: 'Multi-national innovator companies are actively moving to diversify their supply chains, with many looking to shift volume to highly compliant, large-scale Indian contract manufacturing players to de-risk. Divi's and its local peers stand to gain as major drugmakers are diversifying their supply chain to limit their reliance on China.' Also: 'As a dominant pure-play CDMO and API leader, Divi's Laboratories remains uniquely placed to secure high-value long-term contracts under this evolving global framework.' Framed as market opportunity/positioning rather than a specific FY25 revenue-growth attribution in the sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Divi's has 'dependence on raw materials and key intermediates imported from China' and 'concentrated sourcing risk for key inputs -- most notably methanol, imported solvents and Middle-East-sourced materials,' implying petrochemical/solvent-linked exposure, but no specific % of raw material cost was disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports account for roughly 85-90% of sales revenue. One source: 'Exports accounted for 90% of total sales revenue, with Europe and the US contributing 74%.' Another: 'North America contributes ~35-45%, Europe ~30-40%, Rest of World ~20-30%' (of exports/revenue, precise base unclear). Given ambiguity between sources, precise USD-specific % not confidently determined.

rural.evidence: Pidilite refers to rural/semi-urban markets as 'Emerging India' in its MD&A commentary; 'growth in Emerging India continued to be higher than in Urban Markets' (Q1 FY25 commentary). Exact rural revenue % not found in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Vinyl Acetate Monomer (VAM), a crude oil derivative, accounts for approximately 30% of Pidilite's overall raw material costs per one analysis (another source cites 35-40%); VAM price movements (e.g., USD 2,600/tonne to USD 2,000/tonne) materially affect gross margins, with the company historically passing through roughly 75% of raw-material price increases to customers.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports contributed approximately ₹993 Cr in FY25 revenue, roughly 6.5-7.3% of total consolidated revenue per third-party analysis; B2B export segment cited as a growth driver alongside domestic B2B in FY25 commentary. No specific USD-denominated revenue % or hedging policy found in sources reviewed.

rural.evidence: IHCL cites Tier 2 and 3 cities and new industrial corridors as emerging strong demand clusters, though no rural revenue percentage was disclosed in sources reviewed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: IHCL reported minimal significant debt except lease liabilities as of September 30, 2024, with unencumbered cash and liquid investments of over Rs. 2,400 crore.

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst commentary indicates Navin Fluorine is 'benefiting from China+1 sentiment in global supply chain diversification, with rising preference for Indian fluorochemical suppliers'; Specialty Chemicals and CDMO together accounted for ~51% of total exports in H1FY26, but no direct AR MD&A quote attributing revenue growth explicitly to China+1 was located.

crude_exposure.evidence: Company has dependence on imported raw materials like fluorspar and is exposed to energy price movements which can impact margins (fluorspar/HF feedstock, not crude oil directly).

china_plus_one.evidence: Aurobindo targets reducing third-party API dependency to below 20% for its top 50 products through vertical integration; PLI-backed investments (Penicillin-G, 7-ACA, Erythromycin Thiocyanate via Lyfius Pharma) aim to reduce dependence on single-country (China) sourcing, framed around cost/security rather than explicit customer-driven revenue growth from China+1.

pli_scheme.evidence: Aurobindo Pharma (via step-down subsidiary Lyfius Pharma) received PLI scheme approval for Penicillin-G and 7-ACA bulk drug manufacturing at Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh, with committed investment of ~Rs 2,500 crore; commercial production of Penicillin-G ramping up in FY25. Also approved for Erythromycin Thiocyanate (TIOC).

china_plus_one.evidence: Sona continues to gain market share in its top three markets of North America, India and the European Union; recent growth was led by North America (45%) driven by improved EV orders, and Europe growth led by hybrid vehicle sales pick-up. No explicit China+1 framing found, but export/EV order momentum is emphasized. Net order book stood at ~Rs 233 billion with 79% from EV programs.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Rating agency commentary (India Ratings) notes the company mitigates forex risk via 'an effective hedging policy'; specific hedge ratios/instruments not disclosed in sources reviewed.
inr_exposure.evidence: 12%-15% of raw material requirements are imported (mainly from China), exposing the company to forex fluctuation risk, mitigated to a certain extent by the company's effective hedging policy.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona Comstar became the first Indian auto-component manufacturer to receive PLI scheme certification, for a traction motor for electric two-wheelers, followed by additional certifications for traction motors for electric three-wheelers.

china_plus_one.evidence: Secondary-source summary (not primary AR text): Alivus Life Sciences (formerly Glenmark Life Sciences), under Nirma Group ownership, is described as benefiting from the 'China Plus One' globalization trend relevant to its API and CDMO segments; regulated markets (US/EU/Japan/LatAm) contributed ~85% of FY25 revenue vs ~15% from emerging markets, with CDMO (6% of revenue) cited as growing on new project wins.

GSK Pharmaceuticals Ltd (India) is a predominantly domestic formulations business selling in the Indian market; no export or China+1/supply-chain-diversification narrative was found. Could not confirm exact domestic/export split from a primary source (AR PDF at india-pharma.gsk.com was unreachable via available tools).

From Lupin's Integrated Report 2024-25 (business review, via search synthesis): 'Lupin's API and CDMO businesses reflect strong alignment with global industry trends such as supply chain diversification, CDMO outsourcing, and high-potency APIs... ensuring secure global supply chains and elevating India's stature in the global API and CDMO landscape.' No explicit 'China+1' phrase found, but diversification/CDMO-outsourcing framing is present alongside strong US export momentum (US FY25 sales USD 925mn vs USD 815mn FY24).

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Layered hedging strategy combining natural hedges and forex derivatives/forward contracts to manage USD-INR, EUR-INR, and ZAR-INR exposure
inr_exposure.evidence: 'Lupin operates in 100+ markets which exposes it to currency fluctuations, particularly those of USD-INR, EUR-INR, and ZAR-INR. While natural hedges and forex derivatives are deployed, extreme currency movements can impact profitability. Lupin's treasury operations actively monitor exposures and adopt layered hedging strategies.' (Lupin Integrated Report 2024-25, Financial Capital section, via search synthesis)

china_plus_one.evidence: IGI is a gemological certification/grading services business (not a manufacturer/exporter of goods). Its footprint spans India (largest revenue contributor, >80% of CY24 revenue and ~95% of EBITDA), USA, China, Belgium, UAE, Egypt, Israel, Thailand, Hong Kong and Turkiye. No China+1 supply-chain-diversification narrative found; company is described as global leader in lab-grown diamond certification with ~65% market share, but this is a market-share/services narrative, not a manufacturing diversification one.

Titan is an overwhelmingly domestic-market jewellery/watches/eyewear retailer (Tanishq, Mia, CaratLane, Zoya); jewellery division revenue was ₹46,571 crore in FY25 (+21% YoY), almost entirely from India. International jewellery business (via CaratLane's Oct-2024 US entry and a few Middle East Tanishq stores) is nascent -- International jewellery grew 49% YoY to ₹554 crore in Q1FY25, a small fraction of total revenue. No China+1 narrative; company is reportedly exploring Gulf/GCC as a future manufacturing/export hub amid US-India trade tensions, but this is forward-looking, not a current disclosed China+1 driver.

rural.evidence: Company commentary (secondary source) references a strategic pivot toward deeper penetration into Tier-2/3/4/5 towns to unlock potential in smaller markets, but no quantified rural/small-town revenue percentage was found.
